newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee soars to new highs, uptrend continues.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee soars to new highs, uptrend continues.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures continued their uptrend on Tuesday, as heavy speculative buying lifted prices to fresh contract highs across-the-board, traders said.
"The market is fundamentally and technically positive," said Refco Inc analyst Ann Prendergast. "I cannot think of anything exerting a negative influence on prices."

Nearby March delivery surged to a new life-of-contract high of 166.50 cents per lb before a bout of commission house profit-taking trimmed gains. At the close, March stood at 163.55 cents, up 4.90 cents a lb on the day. The session low was 157.50.
Second-position May ended 3.10 cents higher, at 157.55 cents. The March/May spread widened to 6.00 cents compared with 4.20 cents at the close Monday.
Traders said the market received a boost from news a leading U.S. roaster raised retail prices.
Concerns a state workers strike in Colombia could disrupt coffee exports at a time when U.S. inventories are low also fueled the rally, they added.

Procter and Gamble's Folgers Coffee Co said Tuesday it planned to raise the list price on its standard 13-ounce can of coffee by 15 cents effective March 17, due to higher prices of green coffee on the world's futures markets.
"I suppose it (Folgers price hike) is a confirmation of the shortage they perceive," said Prendergast. "But a price rise can limit gains because it can limit consumption."

In Colombia, union leaders representing 800,000 state workers launched a nationwide strike on Tuesday. Although its impact on the coffee sector was not clear, Colombian exporters said they feared the strike could hit customs operations and hold up shipments from some ports.
"The Colombia strike is agitating the market," Prendergast said. "It may not be a long-term thing, but in the short-term it probably will mean delays."
Technically, traders pegged near-term March chart resistance at 167.25, followed by 169.75 and 174.25. To the downside, support was seen at today's low of 157.50, then 155.00.
Volume was heavy, at an estimated 16,050 lots, up from Monday's official tally of 14,678 lots.
